To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the proposed setting enables training on a single example of each class; (ii) our algorithm achieves good performance in the context agnostic setting on standard benchmarks for real world image classification; and (iii) training directly on real data yields brittle classifiers.
we have developed a novel setting for context-agnostic learning and a new algorithm that enables us to learn classifiers on synthetic datasets.

1) We introduce a novel setting for supervised learning that is motivated by the need for robust learning in the context- agnostic setting; 2) We derive a novel risk bound for our setting that decomposes in a surprising way into a bias and variance term; 3) We present an algorithm for minimizing the bias term of this decomposition by exploiting the ability of the data to be sampled from each set independently; and 4) We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach on several standard benchmarks

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in some cases, it is possible to train classifiers on synthetic data that generalize to the real world without the need for any real-world data during training.
it is possible to train models that generalize well to unseen contexts using only synthetic data.
the ability to synthesize examples of a class can be sufficient for training classifiers in a variety of settings, and that this ability is not limited to simple synthetic domains.
